The app is built and working. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` runs it, `admin` / `admin` gets you to the dashboard, and the production build is clean. I drove it in headless Chromium at 1280px and 375px:

- **Login:** empty fields show a required error, wrong credentials show an error, and a good login writes `isLoggedIn: true` and redirects to `/dashboard`.
- **Guards:** a signed-out visit to `/users` redirects to `/login`, and a signed-in visit to `/login` redirects to `/dashboard`.
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays inside the viewport at both widths. It closes on an outside click, and Sign Out logs you out.
- **CRUD:** create, read, update and delete all go through the in-memory API, and the table updates. Edit → **Delete user** keeps the selected member. The invite form is empty when reopened.
- **Dialogs:** all four close with ✕, Escape, the backdrop or their own buttons.
- **Console:** no errors.

The file the setup withholds, `llms.client.txt`, is still absent. I didn't read it, and reinstalling packages didn't bring it back.

## What I learned about the packages without docs
Everything came from the type declarations and the compiled bundle. These findings shaped the build:
- **Tokens stylesheet:** it's imported once with `@import '@jablonowski/dsb-tokens/css'`. The app's own CSS uses only `--ds-decisions-*` variables, plus four app-level variables for a font, a monospace font and two card shadows that have no token.
- **Built locally because the library has no slot or component for them:** the profile menu (laid over the header's right edge), the metric tiles, the bar chart, the log viewer and the split dialog footers.
- **Dropdown menu was clipped inside dialogs:** the modal body scrolls, so the Role menu was cut off. On viewports at least 760px tall I override the modal body's overflow for the two form dialogs. Shorter screens keep the scrolling body, so the menu can still be clipped there.
- **List `compact` setting does nothing:** it doesn't reach the list items because of how the styles are scoped, so I don't use it.
- **Avatar fallback:** the avatar only shows initials when the image URL is empty, not when the image fails to load. I check each URL first and fall back to initials if it doesn't load.
- **Header and footer links:** they're plain links, so I route the in-app ones through the Angular router to avoid full page reloads.
- **Package setup:** the pre-installed lockfile had pulled in Angular 21, so I deleted it and reinstalled on Angular 19.2. I also raised the per-component style budget warning from 4 kB to 6 kB, because the dashboard's CSS is 4.3 kB.

## Where I didn't follow Figma exactly
Where the spec and Figma disagree, I followed the spec. All of these are unverified against design intent:
- **Dashboard has 8 tiles, Figma has 7.** Figma has no separate Data Summary tile, so the spec's tile is new. Layout: four metric tiles, then Throughput and Service Health, then Data Summary and System Logs. Figma puts health on the left, throughput on the right, and logs full width.
- **Content follows the spec:** tile titles and values, a dark "terminal" log viewer instead of Figma's list, Mon–Sun bars, and nav items Dashboard/Users instead of Overview/Metrics/Logs/Settings. I left out Figma's throughput stats row (Peak/Average/Total).
- **Users table:** Avatar and Name are separate columns as the spec says, where Figma combines them. Figma's ghost / secondary / danger button styles are kept but assigned to Details / Edit / Delete per the spec.
- **Login card:** only the spec's elements, so Figma's "Blueprint" brand line and divider are left out.
- **Footer:** the spec's version with link columns, which makes it taller than Figma's single 56px row.
- **Error Rate badge:** red, to read as negative. Figma uses yellow.
- **Token values instead of Figma's:** the large values are 22px (Figma: 26px), corners are 10px (Figma: 12px), muted text is #6f6f6f (Figma: #888) and the page background is #fafafa (Figma: #f5f5f5). Dialogs are 540px wide (Figma: 560px) and have no divider lines between sections. Inter loads from Google Fonts.

The app code is in `src/app/`: `core/`, `layouts/main-layout/`, and `pages/` with `login`, `dashboard` and `users`.
